overall_impact: One demonstrated invalid affine-chart implication in a proof on the core associativity dependency path. Exact restricted-fibre repair verified; no counterexample to the lemma/main theorem demonstrated.

findings.title: Torsion-free group completion does not imply global geometric injectivity of saturation

location.primary: Lemma 8.4, proof Step 3, p.142; Step 4; Theorem 8.12 Step 1 p.152

findings.source_claim: From P=Q+_R^fine Rlambda embedded in torsion-free Qgp, conclude Spec k[Psat] -> Spec k[P] is one-to-one on geometric points.
findings.complete_check: k=C, Q=N e1+N e2, delta=e2, ellq=ell=2e1+mu e2, mu>=1, lambda=mu+2N for N>=1; R=Ndelta+Nell and Rlambda=Ndelta+N(ell-lambda delta) have identical group completions. P=N e1+N e2+N(2e1-2N e2), sharp with functional (a,b)->(N+1)a+b; Psat=N e2+N(e1-N e2), determinant -1. k[P]=k[x,y,z]/(x^2-y^(2N)z), k[Psat]=k[y,t], x=y^N t,z=t^2. Distinct (0,+1),(0,-1) map to (0,0,1).
findings.assumption_boundary: All displayed local algebraic hypotheses of the asserted global chart implication are verified; the offending point is explicitly not in the actual closed-monomial moduli fibre. No geometric punctured-map counterexample is asserted.
findings.counterevidence: Actual Rlambda positive monomials vanish, so z=1 is excluded. The required unique closed geometric lift is true; the paper also explicitly warns in footnote 8 p.140 that the nonreduced map need not be an isomorphism. The surrounding paragraph fixes a geometric ghost stalk, so the sentence admits a valid intended reading restricted to its closed characteristic point. The finding concerns the explicitly written global chart premise, not a failure of that actual restricted conclusion.

repair.statement: A sharp fine P in a torsion-free common group has precisely one geometric point of Spec k[Psat] above the closed monomial point of Spec k[P].
repair.proof: For every nonzero q in Psat, some mq is nonzero in P. At any geometric lift (chi^q)^m=0, hence chi^q=0. Sending all positive monomials to zero exists for a sharp monoid. Both factor ghosts in the actual fine product vanish at the chosen geometric point, so this applies after chart/torsor trivialization. Combined with the already established finite-surjectivity it gives the required bijection.
repair.limits: Does not prove global injectivity, an isomorphism of nonreduced spaces, or arbitrary multiplicity preservation.

findings.dependency: Step 3 -> Lemma 8.4 Step 4 and (1) -> Theorem 8.12 Step 1 -> Theorem 4.28 -> Theorem 4.4 -> Theorems 1.9/1.15.

focused_acceptance.reason: For Q=N e1+N e2, delta=e2, ell=2e1+mu e2, lambda=mu+2N with mu,N>=1, the relevant fine pushout P=<e1,e2,2e1-2Ne2> is sharp in the torsion-free common group, and Psat=<e2,e1-Ne2>. Its saturation map is (y,t)->(x=y^N t,y,z=t^2), with k[P]=k[x,y,z]/(x^2-y^(2N)z). Distinct (0,1) and (0,-1) map to (0,0,1), refuting global geometric injectivity under the displayed local algebraic assumptions. The surrounding text fixes a ghost stalk, and z=1 is excluded from the actual closed monomial fibre; the intended restricted reading is valid. For any nonzero q in Psat, mq is nonzero in P, so at a geometric lift of that closed point (chi^q)^m=0 and chi^q=0. This proves exactly the unique lift required after chart/torsor trivialization, not a nonreduced isomorphism or general multiplicity claim. Step 3 supplies Lemma 8.4(1), used in Theorem 8.12 and the associativity chain through 4.28/4.4. The explicit false global premise remains a Major proof-step defect under the contract, with the strong counterevidence and complete restricted-fibre repair recorded.
